page.h1: HTS Chapter 40: Rubber and Articles Thereof — U.S. Exports & Foreign Tariffs

seo.title: U.S. Tire & Rubber Exports by Country and Foreign Tariffs (HTS Ch. 40) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: U.S. rubber exports were $13.89B in 2025, a third of it new tires. Who buys U.S. tires, gaskets and synthetic rubber, and what Canada, Mexico and China charge.

intro:
The U.S. exported **$13.89B** of rubber and rubber goods in 2025, down 3.8% from 2024 and 5% below the 2022 peak of $14.66B. New tires (4011) are a third of it (**33%, $4.58B**): construction, mining and industrial tires ($1.50B), truck and bus tires ($1.45B) and car tires ($1.33B). Rubber gaskets, seals and other parts (4016, $3.33B, led by gaskets at $1.80B) and synthetic rubber (4002, $2.55B: EPDM, butadiene, SBR and halobutyl) follow, with hoses (4009, $1.19B). **Canada ($3.86B) and Mexico ($3.55B) buy 53%**, mostly tires and auto parts; January–August 2026 exports were $9.65B, up 1.2%.

Most of this trade pays no tariff: Canada, Mexico, Chile, Peru and Australia take qualifying U.S. goods free under trade agreements, Japan charges nothing on tires or synthetic rubber, and the EU cut its duties on U.S. rubber goods (4.5% on car tires) to 0% from July 1, 2026. **Canada** charged a 25% counter-surtax on U.S. tires from March 4 to August 31, 2025, and its 2026 surtax list leaves rubber out. **Mexico** raised its general rate on car and farm tires to 35% in 2026, which U.S. tires escape when they meet the USMCA rule of origin. **China** adds 10% to every U.S. good on top of its 7.5–25% rates, and charges anti-dumping duties of **214.9–222.0%** on U.S. EPDM, **75.5%** on halobutyl rubber and **151%** on chloroprene rubber, which keep most U.S. synthetic rubber out.

keyTakeaways: U.S. Chapter 40 exports were $13.89B in 2025 (−3.8%) and $9.65B in January–August 2026 (+1.2%); new tires (4011, $4.58B) and gaskets, seals and other rubber parts (4016, $3.33B) are 57% of the total.

Canada ($3.86B) and Mexico ($3.55B) take qualifying U.S. tires and rubber parts free; Canada's 25% surtax on U.S. tires lasted from March 4 to August 31, 2025, and none of its 2026 surtaxes covers rubber.

Mexico's general tariff on car and farm tires rose to 35% (25–35% on truck tires, 25% on one gasket line) on January 1, 2026, so the USMCA certification of origin now matters more for tires sold to Mexico.

China ($408M, −15.3%) is the one top buyer charging more than in January 2025: 10% extra on every U.S. good, on top of anti-dumping duties of 214.9–222.0% on EPDM (under expiry review, ruling due by December 19, 2026), 75.5% on halobutyl and 151% on chloroprene rubber.
